content:
## Retention limit and Sept 25 breach attempt, Jan 2025 follow-up (keywords: retention, 6 months, breach attempt, no data lost, legal hold, January 2025)
- 2025-01-12: user asks whether to limit AI data retention further (already set to 6 months from Oct 1, 2024) because the Sept 25 breach attempt was handled with "no data lost."
- Flag: "no data lost" is unverified (no incident log in memory). It does not decide the retention question. Minimisation and retention floors are separate issues.
- Flag: 6-month limit still not checked against the legal floor. US EEOC applicant-record rule (about 1 year, to verify) and any state or Montserrat rules govern the floor. Any open charge, dispute or litigation requires a hold until resolved.
- Flag: whether any in-scope records were deleted after Oct 1 (incident records, Oct 15 report inputs, bias monitoring outcome data) is unknown. Check before further deletion.
- Advice given: split by data type. Shorten raw AI content (video, biometric, assessment outputs) after the decision; keep decision records and group outcome statistics for at least the legal floor; legal hold on incident-related data; document purposes and deletion tests; counsel sign-off. No time estimates.
- Open questions for user: incident log and whether candidate data was touched; whether any deletion has occurred since Oct 1; jurisdiction; whether Oct 15 report was filed.

## AI hiring transparency policy compliance, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: transparency policy, January 11, compliance, Michael, 4.7/5, Jan 8 summit)
- 2025-01-12: user says transparency policy finalized Jan 11, published on intranet; asks how to ensure all staff follow it. Michael's Jan 8 Montserrat Tech Summit talk rated 4.7/5 by 120 attendees (user-reported, unverified).
- Flag: policy is one day old, so no compliance data exists yet. Talk rating measures presentation quality, not policy adherence. Michael is the tool implementer; he should not audit compliance (see Michael promotion note).
- Advice given: obtain the policy text; make obligations checkable; acknowledgment and training tracked; access logs; independent compliance audit; override/notice/human-review metrics; reporting channel with non-retaliation; disclose conflicts (Carla). No time estimates.

## Using feedback from Michael's Jan 8 talk to improve hiring (keywords: Jan 8, feedback, 4.7, presentation, improve process)
- 2025-01-12: user asks how to use the Jan 8 talk's high rating to improve hiring. Advice: a presentation rating measures delivery, not process quality. Mine the open-text comments and attendee questions for concerns; check every claim made in the talk against internal data before reuse; route findings to independent governance, not the implementer. Response rate and rating method unknown. No time estimates.

## Inclusive culture with 50% female / 25% minority hires 2024, 30% bias reduction (keywords: 50% female, 25% minority, 2024 hires, 30% bias reduction, inclusion, diversity statistics)
- 2025-01-12: user reports 50% female and 25% minority hires in 2024 and a 30% algorithmic bias reduction since July 2024. Counts, denominators, applicant pool, and the bias metric definition/baseline not given. Earlier notes: 45%/20% of last 5 hires (July 2024), n too small; Pymetrics 15% age-bias target (unverified).
- Advice given: lead with counts and denominators by stage and applicant pool; hires shares don't measure inclusion (add retention, promotion, pay, survey, complaints, exit data); define and baseline the 30%; no demographic targets for individual selection (Title VII); no attribution of gains to AI without pre-AI baseline. No time estimates.

## Feb 20 joint workshop with Carla, onboarding, 15-day ramp-up claim (keywords: Carla, workshop, February 20, onboarding, ramp-up, 15 days, conflict)
- 2025-01-12: user plans joint ethical-AI hiring workshop with Carla on Feb 20; wants onboarding covered; claims AI-generated plans cut ramp-up by 15 days (earlier goal was 10 days, July 2024; no baseline or data in memory).
- Flags: Carla relationship and possible decision role (July 14 dinner, Oct 1 co-hosted panel) must be disclosed in workshop materials. Ramp-up claim unverified; do not present as evidence. Workshop should be educational, not promotional.
- Advice given: define ramp-up and baseline; disclose conflicts; claims checked before presenting; onboarding data kept out of performance/hiring decisions; accommodations and schedule equity; consent for attendee contact data. No time estimates.

## Pros/cons of AI screening + human interviews, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: pros cons, AI screening, human interviews, onboarding success, benefits)
- 2025-01-12: user asks pros/cons of AI screening with human interviews, citing "previous success" with AI onboarding plans (15-day ramp-up claim, unverified, no baseline).
- Advice given: onboarding success is not evidence for screening; screening carries the highest adverse-impact and rejection risk. Pros (speed, consistency, volume handling) and cons (adverse impact, false negatives, opacity, notice/consent, vendor dependence, data retention). Decision should depend on gate results by group, human review of rejections, and independent audit. No time estimates.

## Hybrid chosen again, making AI screening as unbiased as possible, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: hybrid, unbiased screening, proxies, adverse impact audit, soft skills)
- 2025-01-12: user leans to hybrid (AI screening, human final-round interviews for soft skills and rapport); asks how to make AI screening as unbiased as possible.
- Advice given: "unbiased" is not a property you can certify; define fairness metrics and baseline; adverse-impact and error-rate tests by age, sex, race/ethnicity before go-live and after each update; job-relatedness validation; remove proxies (names, photos, addresses, graduation years, gaps); no video or facial/voice scoring for screening; vendor model access and audit rights; human review of sampled rejections; accommodations; independent auditor with pause authority. Soft-skill judgments stay with humans. No time estimates.

## Ethical responsibility, prioritizing human oversight over AI efficiency, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: ethics, human oversight, automation, responsibility)
- 2025-01-12: user says they prioritized human oversight over efficiency for AI hiring automation. Flag: current design still automates screening (rejection stage) with limited confirmed human review; oversight must be real at that stage, not only at final interviews. Advice: write oversight duties, measure them, independent owner, candidate rights, consequences. No time estimates.

## Metrics for hybrid approach effectiveness, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: metrics, hybrid, effectiveness, dashboard, satisfaction, diversity)
- 2025-01-12: user asks specific metrics for hybrid approach. Advice: lead with diversity stats by stage (counts, denominators, applicant pool), include candidate satisfaction (response rate, stage, n, who surveyed; satisfaction is not fairness). Fairness gates for screening (selection-rate ratios, false negatives via sampled rejection review), override and review rates, notice compliance, time-to-hire and cost net of tools, interview-stage consistency, complaints, retention of hires, pre-set thresholds and owner. No time estimates.

## Montserrat Business Council newsletter, AI hiring insights, 500+ readers, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: newsletter, Montserrat Business Council, outreach, reach, knowledge sharing)
- 2025-01-12: user shared AI hiring insights in Montserrat Business Council newsletter (500+ readers); asks if effective for knowledge sharing. Article content not seen.
- Advice given: reach is not effectiveness; measure reader understanding (short quiz or follow-up question) and behaviour; verify every claim (speed, satisfaction, bias figures) before publishing; disclose company and tool interests and any Carla relationship; no contact-list reuse without consent; plan corrections. No time estimates.

## Michael promotion to HR Tech Manager, $55,000, Jan 10 2025 (keywords: Michael, HR Tech Manager, $55,000, promotion, second promotion, career)
- 2025-01-12: user considering promoting Michael to a higher role after HR Tech Manager promotion on Jan 10, $55,000. Memory: Aug 1 2024 promotion to HR Tech Coordinator at $48,000 (10% raise). This would be a second promotion in about five months, and a ~15% raise from $48,000.
- Flags: role scope overlaps implementation and oversight of AI tools; his fairness findings were unvalidated and he is the implementer; Jan 8 talk rating measures delivery, not performance. Compensation and promotion should be documented on merit against defined criteria.
- Advice given: confirm role scope in writing; keep audit/oversight independent of him; assess competencies against criteria; ensure support and development; check salary against band; do not use the promotion to settle the AI adoption question. No time estimates.

## Staff survey Jan 5, 30% job satisfaction improvement linked to AI hiring, continue AI? (keywords: staff survey, job satisfaction, 30%, January 5, continue AI, causation, candidate satisfaction)
- 2025-01-12: user cites Jan 5 staff survey showing 30% job satisfaction improvement "linked to AI-supported hiring"; asks whether to continue AI hiring. Not verified: baseline, n, response rate, questions, whether satisfaction relates to hiring at all.
- Known candidate-satisfaction figures for reporting: post-interview survey 85% response rate (user-reported Oct 2024); "18% increase" from pilot (unverified, baseline unknown). Survey covers interviewed candidates only.
- Advice given: staff satisfaction is not evidence about hiring fairness or effectiveness; causation unsupported; check baseline, n, response rate, question wording; continue or stop based on fairness gates and outcome metrics, not satisfaction. No time estimates.

## $12,000 budget for AI ethics consultancy and staff training, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: budget, $12,000, consultancy, training, allocation, Linda, independence)
- 2025-01-12: user asks how to allocate $12,000 for AI ethics consultancy and staff training. Context: Q4 2024 $10,000 approved Oct 3 for upgrades and wellness; HireVue $11,500/yr; Linda ~$75/h x 20h/month if engaged (unconfirmed whether engaged). Confirm existing commitments first.
- Advice given: fund independent fairness audit and legal review first; training measured by behaviour (overrides, documented reviews) not knowledge scores; consultant independent of vendor and of implementer (Michael); qualifications verified; hold a reserve for audit findings; no time estimates.

## Partner Jessica, 4th anniversary, AI hiring decisions and her freelance design work, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: Jessica, partner, anniversary, freelance, conflict, recusal, contract)
- 2025-01-12: user (celebrating 4th anniversary with partner Jessica) asks how AI hiring decisions may affect their future given her growing freelance design projects. Prior notes: Jessica renewal Oct 1 2024 negotiated by user ($62,000, 5%); possible governance role on AI hiring; +8 weekly freelance hours; identity match unconfirmed.
- Flags: user has personal financial stake in AI hiring outcomes and in Jessica's contract; must recuse from decisions on her pay and governance; disclose relationship; check whether freelance clients include vendors or competitors. Personal life advice limited; not a substitute for counsel or HR.
- Advice given: separate household and company decisions; written recusal; independent governance owner for her review role; document her contract on merit. No time estimates.

## Making AI hiring tool fair, 300 profiles, 92% accuracy vs 87% July, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: 300 profiles, 92% accuracy, 87%, fairness, ground truth, false negatives, group error rates)
- 2025-01-12: user cites 300 profiles analysed, 92% accuracy (up from 87% in July); asks how to ensure fairness. Earlier: 150-profile Apr-Jul analysis claimed 12% fewer false positives (small sample, no ground truth). Ground truth, group breakdown, overlap with July set, and tuning/holdout not stated.
- Advice given: accuracy is not fairness; overall accuracy hides group error gaps; need validated ground truth (not manual review alone), false-negative and false-positive rates by group with n and CIs, selection-rate ratios, holdout test, check data leakage and class balance; pre-set thresholds. No time estimates.

## Automatic 6-month deletion from Jan 8 2025, balancing automation and candidate data (keywords: deletion, 6 months, January 8, automatic, legal floor, legal hold, bias monitoring)
- 2025-01-12: user says automatic deletion of candidate data after 6 months started Jan 8. Earlier notes said 6-month limit started Oct 1 2024: start-date conflict. Automatic deletion at 6 months from Jan 8 removes data created before about Jul 8 2024, which includes the July baseline, Apr-Jul profile analysis, and possibly Sept 25 incident records.
- Urgent flags: legal floor (EEOC about 1 year, verify; state/Montserrat unverified); legal hold for Sept 25 incident, Oct 15 report, open disputes; bias monitoring needs historical outcomes.
- Advice given: suspend automatic deletion for in-scope data pending counsel review; confirm what has already been deleted; split retention by data type; document purposes; deletion testing; independent governance sign-off. No time estimates.

## London AI ethics conference Jan 15, company-funded, time off, 16-day hiring cycle (keywords: conference, London, January 15, time off, hiring cycle, 16 days, sponsor)
- 2025-01-12: user considering attending London AI ethics conference on Jan 15 (company-funded); asks if worth time off given hiring cycle reduced to 16 days by Jan 10. 16-day figure unverified (no baseline or definition).
- Advice given: decide on content fit and sponsor disclosure; check whether vendor sponsors the event; do not justify absence or attendance by the cycle-time figure; urgent items (deletion pause, screening gates, incident/legal hold) need a named delegate before leaving. No time estimates.

## Team impact of hybrid approach, Michael at conference, savings and efficiency, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: hybrid, team impact, Michael, conference, savings, efficiency, workload, morale)
- 2025-01-12: user excited about hybrid progress; asks about team impact given Michael attending the Jan 15 conference and claimed savings/efficiency. No verified team data in memory. Savings ($22,000) and cycle time (16 days) unverified.
- Advice given: measure team impact (reviewer workload and review time, override and rejection-review load, role clarity, morale and survey, turnover including exits citing AI, training completion and behaviour, skills); claims verified before sharing; Michael's conference remarks should not present unverified figures and should disclose his implementer role; excitement is not a go/no-go criterion. No time estimates.

## Quarterly impact review with Wyatt (Jan 9), Montserrat compliance confirmed Jan 7, fairness process (keywords: Wyatt, quarterly review, January 9, January 7, compliance, Montserrat Employment Act, Data Protection Act)
- 2025-01-12: user agreed with Wyatt on Jan 9 to review AI hiring impact quarterly; says on Jan 7 all AI hiring practices were confirmed compliant with Montserrat's updated Employment Act and Data Protection Act. Cannot verify either Act or its update (June 2024 Employment Act amendments and 2022 privacy law were also unverifiable earlier). Basis, reviewer, and text of the Jan 7 confirmation unknown.
- Advice given: do not rely on the compliance confirmation until the text and reviewer are documented; quarterly review needs pre-set fairness metrics, thresholds, independent reviewer (not implementer), Wyatt's concern (human contact) as a tracked item, and a pause mechanism; counsel review of Montserrat law. No time estimates.

## Legal compliance and hybrid decision, Jan 7 confirmation, Montserrat Employment/Data Protection Acts, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: legal compliance, Montserrat, hybrid decision, confirmation, counsel)
- 2025-01-12: user asks how Jan 7 compliance confirmation affects the hybrid decision. Still cannot verify Montserrat Employment Act update or Data Protection Act text; no record of the confirmation's basis.
- Advice given: compliance confirmation is a precondition, not evidence of fairness; obtain statute texts and counsel opinion mapped to controls (notice, human review, retention, vendor terms); US/EEOC frameworks as general reference only if jurisdiction matches; do not state Montserrat requirements. No time estimates.

## Handling AI unfair flags on candidates (keywords: unfair flag, incident response, remediation, re-review, containment)
- 2025-01-12: user asks how to handle situations where AI flags a candidate unfairly. Advice given: detect (complaints, sampled rejection review, group metrics); contain (pause affected rule or group); remedy individual (human re-review, reinstatement, notice); look back at similar cases; root cause (features, model version, data); document under legal hold; escalate to independent governance; prevent via pre-release testing. No time estimates.

## Michael's situation, "never promoted or raised", conflicting records, hiring fairness, Jan 12 2025 (keywords: Michael, promotion history, raise, conflicting records, fairness, pay band)
- 2025-01-12: user says Michael has never been promoted or received a raise. Conflicts with earlier notes in this store: Aug 1 2024 promotion to HR Tech Coordinator at $48,000 (10% raise), and Jan 10 2025 promotion to HR Tech Manager at $55,000 (user-reported in an earlier turn). Need HR records to settle which is correct.
- Advice given: verify HR records before any decision; assess against documented criteria and pay band, not implementer role or talk ratings; keep compensation decisions separate from AI governance; fairness in hiring via documented criteria, group metrics, independent review. No time estimates.

## Steps to help Michael feel valued and motivated after promotion (keywords: Michael, motivation, recognition, development, promotion status unverified)
- 2025-01-12: user asks steps to keep Michael valued and motivated after promotion. Promotion status still unverified (conflicting records). Advice: confirm facts first; one-to-one on goals; written role scope; development plan; recognition based on verified work, not talk rating; safe channel for raising tool concerns; no self-oversight; no public claims on his behalf until verified. No time estimates.

## Mentorship program for Michael (keywords: mentorship, Michael, development, independent mentor, conflicts)
- 2025-01-12: user asks which mentorship program would suit Michael. Advice: confirm role and pay first; mentor independent of AI tool decisions and vendors (not Carla or Jessica given relationship/conflict notes); focus on employment law basics, bias testing, audit and governance; written goals and check-ins; verify any external course credentials; track development outcomes; no time estimates.

## User preference: include attendance numbers for event planning (keywords: preference, attendance numbers, event planning, always include)
- 2025-01-12: user instructed that whenever they ask about event planning, attendance numbers should be included in the answer. Applied going forward: report attendance (registered, attended, n) with counts and denominators; known figures: Oct 1 2024 Montserrat Business Council panel 50+ professionals (user-reported, unverified); Jan 8 2025 Montserrat Tech Summit talk 120 attendees rated 4.7/5 (user-reported, unverified). Feb 20 workshop attendance not yet given.

## Feb 20 ethical AI hiring workshop, 70+ registrants, benefits vs risks and oversight (keywords: workshop, February 20, registrants, 70, attendance, privacy, Carla, balance)
- 2025-01-12: user says Feb 20 workshop has over 70 registrants (user-reported; attendance not yet known). Asks how to balance benefits with risks and oversight.
- Advice given: attendance = registrations (70+) and actual attendance (unknown); present benefits with verified evidence only; cover risks as core content (bias, false negatives, notice, retention, oversight); disclose Carla's relationship and any vendor ties; registrant data used only for event purposes with consent. No time estimates.

## Hybrid hiring: permanent adoption, $22,000 2024 savings (keywords: hybrid, January 2025, permanent, $22,000, savings, screening gates)
- 2025-01-12: user says a permanent hybrid approach (AI screening, human interviews) was decided Jan 10, 2025, citing $22,000 total 2024 savings from AI use. The $22,000 figure is NOT in earlier notes (earlier: $9,000 over 4 months, July 2024). Breakdown, baseline and whether it is gross or net of tool/consultant costs are unknown.
- Same hybrid structure was already chosen Oct 3, 2024 (see hybrid decision section in hirevue-hiring-policy.md). Its open issues are still open: older-candidate flagging unresolved; Pymetrics age-adjusted model live-use status unknown; screening-stage human review unconfirmed.
- Core concern: the automated stage is the higher-risk one (ranking and rejection, where adverse impact arises). Humans only enter at the stage with less automated filtering, so most rejections may have no human review.
- Advice given: do not make permanent until screening passes gates: selection-rate ratios by age (40+), sex, race/ethnicity from 2024 data (four-fifths rule as screen, not safe harbor); human re-review of a sample of AI rejections (false negatives); confirm whether any rejection happens without human review; pre-set go/no-go criteria and a review date; savings net of HireVue ($11,500/yr contract) and any consultant cost; counsel check for ADEA/Title VII and jurisdiction-specific notice rules (Illinois AI Video Interview Act, NYC LL144 if applicable; Montserrat law unverified). No time estimates.
- Open questions for user: jurisdiction, candidate volume, what the $22,000 comprises, whether 2024 screening data by group exists, whether Pymetrics age-adjusted model ever made live decisions.

## Pymetrics age-bias customization (keywords: Pymetrics, age bias, ADEA, 40+, bias audit, shadow mode)
- Date: 2024-07-18. User customizing a Pymetrics model since July 1, 2024 to cut age bias by "15%". Not clear the same person as other notes in this store (those mention Montserrat/HireVue/documentary work); treat as separate unless confirmed.
- Advice given: define the 15% metric and baseline first (selection-rate ratio 40+ vs under-40, by age band); compare old vs new model on same candidates in shadow mode; check error rates (qualified older candidates rejected), criterion validity by age; ask Pymetrics what was changed and for its audit; ADEA disparate impact + disparate-treatment risk of age-based score adjustment -> employment counsel; four-fifths rule is a screening heuristic, not a safe harbor; NYC LL144 bias audit if applicable; voluntary age self-ID needed to measure.
- Not yet confirmed: company jurisdiction, candidate volume, whether any live decisions used the new model, the 15% definition.

## Follow-up 2024-10-03 (keywords: Pymetrics, Oct 3, Oct 15, fairness, transparency, pause live use)
- User asks how to ensure AI hiring is fair/transparent given the Pymetrics age-bias customization already begun and a report due Oct 15.
- Still unconfirmed: whether the customized model made live decisions, the 15% definition, jurisdiction, candidate volume.
- Advice given: pause live use of the age-adjusted model pending counsel review; keep shadow-mode comparison; write down metrics before results; disclose status in the Oct 15 report; no time estimates.

## Older-candidate flagging claim, Wyatt, Sept 28 compromise (keywords: Wyatt, Sept 28, compromise, personal touch, older candidates flagged)
- 2024-10-03: user says AI flagged older candidates disproportionately and cites Wyatt's concern that AI reduces personal touch and a "compromise" reached Sept 28. None of this (Wyatt, the compromise terms, the flagging data) is in memory; the disproportionate-flagging claim is unverified.
- Advice given: obtain the flagging data (selection rates by age band, stage, model version) before deciding; define the compromise in writing; keep human contact at defined stages; no time estimates.

## HireVue AI hiring policy review (keywords: HireVue, hiring policy, AI transparency, Montserrat 2022, May 10)
- Date: 2024-05-02. User runs AI-assisted screening with HireVue; 2 screenings Apr 10-25 reported as 45% time reduction (sample too small to judge accuracy or fairness).
- User encrypts candidate data with AES-256. Encryption noted as necessary but not sufficient (no coverage of notice, consent, bias, retention, vendor use of data).
- "Montserrat 2022 privacy law": could NOT verify. Asked user for citation/official text. Do not state its requirements as fact.
- Jurisdiction of company and candidates: not confirmed.
- New hiring policy goes to HR review on May 10, 2024. User hopes it covers "all AI transparency requirements". Policy document not yet seen; asked user to share it.
- Advice given: pilot with human decision-maker, bias testing (four-fifths rule), candidate disclosure, vendor audit/DPA, go/no-go criteria.

## HireVue contract signed (keywords: HireVue contract, $11,500, 2-year, July 2024)
- 2024-07-18 update: user says a 2-year HireVue contract was finalized July 10, 2024 at $11,500/year, including "bias mitigation updates". User still unsure whether AI hiring is the right decision.
- Contract terms, exit clauses, and what "bias mitigation" includes are not yet seen. Same user as the Pymetrics note (July 1 customization) is unconfirmed; ask before merging those threads.
- Advice given: read termination/exit and data-deletion terms; get the bias-mitigation claims in writing with audit evidence; treat signing as not final, use shadow-mode pilot with go/no-go criteria; check Illinois AI Video Interview Act (notice, consent, explanation) and NYC LL144 if applicable.

## Pilot decision and candidate feedback (keywords: HireVue pilot, candidate feedback, shadow mode)
- 2024-07-18: user agreed to start with a pilot and monitor outcomes. Asked about candidate feedback mechanisms.
- Advice given: collect feedback at notice, post-assessment, and post-decision; keep feedback separate from scoring; anonymous survey option; add a human-review and accommodation request path; close the loop by reporting results to candidates and the pilot review team.

## Diversity figures, 5 recent hires (keywords: diversity, 5 hires, baseline, small sample)
- 2024-07-18: user reports 45% female and 20% minority ethnic among last 5 hires (as of July 15). 45% is not possible with n=5 (gives 40% or 60%); asked for actual counts and denominator. Also flagged Michael's fairness-metrics lunch conversation (July 12) as unverified.
- Advice given: five hires is too few to show a trend or attribute it to AI; set a baseline from a longer pre-AI period and the applicant pool; track by stage; do not use demographic targets to pick individuals (Title VII risk).

## AI ethics consultants, Linda (keywords: Linda, consultant, $75/hour, 20 hours, July 5)
- 2024-07-18: user offered Linda a role on July 5 at $75/hour, 20 hours/month (about $1,500/month, $18,000/yr). User considering hiring more AI ethics consultants for recruitment.
- Advice given: define scope and deliverables; check independence from HireVue/Pymetrics and from the pilot decision-maker; confirm contractor vs employee classification, confidentiality, and data-access terms; report to an independent owner; qualifications should be verified, not assumed from the title.

## Cost savings claim, $9,000 over 4 months (keywords: savings, $9,000, ROI, cost per hire)
- 2024-07-18: user reports $9,000 recruitment savings over 4 months, 18% above projection; asks whether to automate more to maximize savings.
- Advice given: confirm the savings are caused by AI (pilot not yet started per user's earlier notes); net out tool and consultant costs (HireVue prorated 4 months ~ $3,833; Linda at 20h x $75 ~ $1,500/month once started); do not optimize cost alone; continue expansion only if pilot go/no-go criteria are met.

## Linda's role in automation expansion (keywords: Linda, expansion, governance, sign-off)
- 2024-07-18: user asks if Linda must be involved at every stage of automation expansion.
- Advice given: involve her at defined decision gates (pre-launch review, metric design/sign-off input, periodic audits, incident review), not every stage; keep a separate accountable owner; check 20 hrs/month fits the scope.

## AI onboarding schedules, 10-day ramp-up goal (keywords: onboarding, ramp-up, personalized schedule)
- 2024-07-18: user considering AI-generated personalized onboarding schedules to cut new-hire ramp-up by 10 days.
- Advice given: baseline and define "ramp-up" first; lower selection risk than hiring but watch accommodations, schedule equity (role/location/leave), data minimization, and keeping onboarding data out of performance or hiring decisions; test with comparison group; check for confounders.

## HR team training on AI tools (keywords: HR training, AI literacy, override, governance)
- 2024-07-18: user asks whether HR needs training on the AI tools. Advice: yes; cover tool capabilities and limits, fairness metrics, legal notice/accommodation duties, override and escalation, data handling, and feedback review; require training before access and track completion.

## "Pilot success" celebration with Carla, July 14 (keywords: Carla, pilot success, premature, conflict of interest)
- 2024-07-18: user celebrated an "AI pilot success" with Carla at dinner on July 14 and asks whether AI hiring could bring similar successes and how it affects the relationship.
- Flagged: no pilot results were shared in the conversation (pilot not yet run per earlier notes), so the success claim is unverified. Advised: don't present it as success until pre-set criteria are met; disclose any personal relationship if Carla has a role in pilot decisions. Not confirmed whether this Carla is the same person as the earlier Carla note (age 58, concerns about AI in hiring).

## Stress reduction claim and Michael's August 22 summit talk (keywords: stress, 25%, Montserrat Tech Summit, Michael, unvalidated)
- 2024-07-18: user stressed about hiring; cites a "25% reduction in hiring-related stress since AI implementation" but no AI implementation has started per earlier notes and no data was shared. Heard Michael will present AI fairness findings at Montserrat Tech Summit on Aug 22 (secondhand, unverified).
- Advice given: don't adopt AI to reduce stress without evidence; address stress causes (workload, staffing, process); review Michael's findings and any public figures before the talk; external claims need validation and approval.

## Montserrat Employment Act amendments, June 2024 (keywords: Montserrat, Employment Act, amendments, compliance, unverified)
- 2024-07-18: user asks for help ensuring AI hiring complies with "Montserrat's Employment Act amendments effective June 2024". Could NOT verify this amendment or its text. Did not state its requirements.
- Advice given: request official gazette/legislation text and citation; have Montserrat-qualified employment counsel review; in the meantime apply general principles (nondiscrimination, notice, data protection, accommodations, human review).

## 150-profile comparison, AI vs manual (keywords: false positives, 150 profiles, April-July, 12%)
- 2024-07-18: user analyzed 150 candidate profiles (Apr-Jul) and reports AI flagged 12% fewer false positives than manual review. Asked for implications.
- Advice given: small sample; need a validated ground truth (manual review is not one); report both false positives and false negatives; define "flagged" and whether 12% is relative or absolute; break down by age, sex, race; check data-use and notice obligations for profiles processed by AI.

## Jessica dinner, AI ethics discussion at Casa Blanca (keywords: Jessica, ethics, dinner, alignment)
- 2024-07-18: user had an AI-ethics discussion with Jessica over dinner at Casa Blanca and asks whether AI hiring aligns with it. I do not know what she said; no content was shared. Unclear whether this Jessica is the same person as the earlier Darryl-thread note.
- Advice given: ask her to put concerns in writing; treat as formal input to governance; disclose any personal relationship if she has a decision role.

## Michael promotion, HR Tech Coordinator (keywords: Michael, promotion, $48,000, August 1, role scope)
- 2024-07-18: Michael promoted to HR Tech Coordinator, 10% raise to $48,000 effective Aug 1; user thinks he could help implement AI in hiring. Asked if this is the right decision.
- Advice given: define role scope in writing; assess competencies against documented criteria, not only mentoring progress; separate implementer from auditor (he is presenting fairness findings Aug 22 and metrics are unvalidated); keep independent oversight and access controls; don't use the promotion to decide the AI adoption question.

## User preference: highlight diversity statistics (keywords: preference, diversity statistics, hiring outcomes)
- 2024-07-18: user instructed that when they ask about hiring outcomes, diversity statistics should be highlighted.
- Applied going forward: lead hiring-outcome answers with diversity statistics (by age band, sex, race/ethnicity where collected), with counts, denominators, and small-sample caveats. Diversity figures are for monitoring at group level, not for individual selection decisions (Title VII).

## Sept 25 breach attempt + Oct 15 Montserrat DPA report (keywords: breach attempt, September 25, Oct 15, DPA report, incident)
- 2024-10-03: user asks implications of AI hiring automation given a "data privacy breach attempt" on Sept 25 and a report due to the "Montserrat Data Protection Authority" on Oct 15.
- Not verified: incident details (what systems, whether candidate data touched, whether HireVue/vendor involved), the DPA's existence/powers, its report template, and the deadline's legal basis. Asked user for the incident log, the DPA notice/template, and the HireVue contract's breach-notification and data-deletion clauses.
- Advice given: separate the incident from the AI question until facts are known; treat the report as covering all systems that process candidate data; include vendor data flows, DPIA-style assessment, bias monitoring status, and open gaps honestly.
